formulas.formula: Your fixed income, your bills and your health costs. Clear, calm and in large print.
1. Setup: your name, birth year, savings, and expected growth and inflation.
2. Income: Social Security, pension and other income. It takes out taxes and Medicare to show what you really get.
3. Budget: plan each category for one month. Yearly bills are set aside automatically.
4. Transactions: write down what you spend. Pick a category from the list.
5. Yearly Bills: property tax, insurance and other once-a-year bills. See how much to set aside each month.
6. Nest Egg: see how long your savings last with the withdrawals you take.
7. Health & Rx: your medicines, refill dates and doctor visits, all in one place.
Everything is in big, easy-to-read type. Zoom in more with Ctrl and + if you like.
When income doesn't change, the budget is your raise. Small cuts add up.
Setting a little aside each month means no surprises when big bills come.
Many planners suggest taking about 4% of your savings a year.
Clear the white cells on Income, Budget, Transactions, Yearly Bills and Health & Rx.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Red: over budget, overdue, or something to check.
